name: Liên Đoàn Kateri Tekakwitha
affiliation: Vietnamese Eucharistic Youth Movement in Canada
introduction: United in the Eucharist. Growing in faith, friendship, and service across our Vietnamese Catholic communities in Ontario.
about: Since 2013, TNTT chapters across Ontario have worked together to help young people live like Jesus and deepen their relationship with him. Through team life, meetings, music, liturgy, retreats, and camps, members have opportunities to reflect, share experiences, serve others, and discern their Christian vocations.
history:
Their collaboration began with the first Nghĩa sĩ Retreat at the Martyrs’ Shrine in Midland in 2013. It grew to include Bethsaida, an annual retreat and formation program for Hiệp Sĩ in Ontario and Québec; Tabor, an annual retreat for Huynh trưởng and Hiệp sĩ Trưởng Thành; and two summer camps for đoàn sinh from across Ontario. Local Chapter Executive Committees (Ban Chấp hành Đoàn) organized these programs with Huynh trưởng who took on additional planning and coordination.

Over the next five years, chapters in Ontario and Québec worked within a structure similar to a League of Chapters Council (Hội đồng Liên đoàn) and Executive Committee (Ban Chấp hành Liên đoàn). Drawing on that experience, the National Executive Committee proposed an amendment to the TNTT Canada Charter (Bản Nội quy) to define the League of Chapters structure and the boundaries of four leagues.

The amendment passed in 2019, and Liên đoàn Kateri Tekakwitha was formally established on July 14, 2019, at the Nghĩa-Hiệp Conference at Mount Mary Retreat Centre in Hamilton. An Interim Executive Committee was appointed to prepare resolutions for selecting the patron saint and setting June 20, 2020, as the election date for the 2020–2023 League Executive Committee.

As of 2026, Liên đoàn Kateri has seven đoàn across three dioceses in Ontario:

- Archdiocese of Toronto
  - Đoàn Tôma Thiện Toronto
  - Đoàn Têrêsa Hài Đồng Scarborough
  - Đoàn Emmanuel North York
  - Đoàn Anrê Dũng Lạc Mississauga
- Diocese of Hamilton
  - Đoàn Phanxicô Xaviê Cần Hamilton
  - Đoàn Anrê Phú Yên Kitchener-Waterloo
- Diocese of London
  - Đoàn Anê Thành Windsor
patronText:
St. Kateri Tekakwitha was born in 1656 in what is now New York State to a Mohawk father and a Christian Algonquin mother. When she was four, a smallpox epidemic took the lives of her parents and younger brother. Kateri survived, but the illness left her with facial scars and impaired vision. Her uncle and other relatives raised her in the Mohawk community.

Kateri learned about Christianity from Jesuit missionaries and was baptized by Father Jacques de Lamberville on April 18, 1676. She faced opposition from some members of her community because of her faith and her decision to remain unmarried. She later moved to the Mission of St. Francis Xavier near present-day Montréal, where she could practice her faith more freely.

Prayer, service, and devotion to Jesus in the Eucharist shaped Kateri’s life. On March 25, 1679, she made a vow of perpetual virginity. She died on April 17, 1680. Tradition records her final words as “Jesus, I love you.” Her courage and faith continue to inspire people today.
